key_insight: A simple reconstruction pretraining stage can make one-step generative models much easier to train, removing much of the difficulty of later distributional optimization.
engineering_relevance: Priming Models offer a lower-compute path to high-quality one-step generation, improving the training-compute versus sample-quality tradeoff for image and world-model generation.
method: Train first with a reconstruction objective, such as pixel-space denoising at a fixed noise level.
Then fine-tune in feature space with distributional post-training.
Use this two-stage setup to prime the model before one-step generation training.
evidence_signal: Across class-conditional image generation, text-to-image generation, and world modeling, the method improves the training-compute/quality Pareto frontier and reaches FID 1.19 on ImageNet 256×256 with about one-tenth the training compute of comparable prior one-step methods.
watch_item: Results may depend on careful design of the priming reconstruction task and on whether the downstream feature-space post-training transfers well across domains.
